clue.text: Point creature's head out

indicators.note: with its head out, a word loses its first letter and keeps the rest

blocks.note: a creature is a beast; its first letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone points out a creature poking its head out of a burrow.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAST loses its B to leave EAST. 'Point' here is a compass point, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal directions marked on a compass.

clue.text: Old lady eating one's bread

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: a nan is a grandmother, an old lady

explanation.surface: A grandmother tucks into someone's loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: NAN takes in A to make NA(A)N. The 's is 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a flat leavened loaf from South Asian cooking, baked in a tandoor.

clue.text: Guy drinks noisily

indicators.note: done noisily means heard rather than seen, so the sound is what counts

blocks.note: cups of tea are drinks; said out loud the plural matches the answer

explanation.surface: A man slurps his drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a noun for a man, but it is the verb meaning to mock or rib.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to make fun of them, the same as ribbing or mocking them playfully.

clue.text: Government official gets a rise (slightly less than fifty percent)

indicators.note: a little under half of some letters is taken, so a short run sits inside a longer string

blocks.note: four consecutive letters from the middle of these nine

explanation.surface: A civil servant gets a pay rise, though under half of what was asked.
explanation.walkthrough: The parenthesis looks like a pay figure, but it counts letters: four out of the nine in 'gets a rise'.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers call a government-appointed head of a policy area, like a drugs chief, by this Russian imperial title.

clue.text: Excellent knockout I'd welcomed in self-defence

indicators.note: a guest who is welcomed is taken in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the letter I for the digit

explanation.surface: A fighter delighted to have landed a knockout while defending themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning first-rate, is written with the letter I standing in for the digit 1, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese martial art built on turning an attacker's force aside rather than striking.

clue.text: Primate's rage directed at band

indicators.note: letters that are directed are ordered about into a new arrangement

blocks.note: a band is a strip of tape

explanation.surface: An ape's fury is aimed at a group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' reads as a group of players but is a strip of sticky material; 'at' simply joins the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas, chimpanzees and orangutans are the large tailless members of the monkey order.

clue.text: Soldiers knocked over - that's horrible part of course

indicators.note: something knocked over ends up upside down, which in a down clue flips the order

explanation.surface: Troops scattered on a racecourse or assault course, an awful sight.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the standard crossword abbreviation for Other Ranks. The 'course' is a golf course, not a race or a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf layout the long grass bordering the fairway is where wayward shots land.

clue.text: Looking happy - agreed about keeping money I left

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
to keep something is to hold it, so one piece holds others inside

explanation.surface: Someone grins after a deal on the money they are owed.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for agreeing is turned round first, and only then wraps the money, the I and the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley face or expression is one wearing a grin, cheerful in appearance.

clue.text: Cause to love early Corrie legend (special one)? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means lose half, so only the first half of a name stays

blocks.note: Ena Sharples, a formidable character from the first years of Coronation Street
Jose Mourinho, the football manager who called himself the Special One

explanation.surface: A soap veteran and a famous football manager supposedly make you fall in love.
explanation.walkthrough: Corrie is Coronation Street, the long-running British TV soap. Only the first four letters of the eight-letter MOURINHO are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour someone is to charm them into affection, making them fond or smitten.

clue.text: Car one American can make

explanation.surface: A car that any American could build.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' looks like a car maker; it only links the parts to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Austin was a British motor manufacturer whose models, like the Mini and Seven, bore its name.

clue.text: Still being here, take car outside (can I get into reverse?)

indicators.note: to be outside something is to surround it, so one piece wraps another
going into reverse gear means travelling backwards, and the letters run backwards too

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take
can is slang for a toilet, as is lav

explanation.surface: A driver who is still here asks whether they can put the car in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take' is R because doctors' prescriptions began with R for recipe, Latin for take. 'Can' is slang for a toilet, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Survival is the state of continuing to live or exist after danger has passed.

clue.text: B1 unconvincing about China according to Macron

indicators.note: to be about something is to be around it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: china means mate in rhyming slang (china plate); the French president would say ami

explanation.surface: A weak comment on China by the French president.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, and ami is French for friend. B1 looks like a code but is a vitamin.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitamin B1 is the chemical name of this nutrient, found in grains and needed for metabolism.

clue.text: Hard for regulars to make trouble

indicators.note: things that come at regular intervals suggest taking every second letter

blocks.note: the even letters of these two words

explanation.surface: It's hard for the regular customers to cause a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regulars' reads as pub customers but asks for the second, fourth and sixth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: Child is a girl

explanation.surface: Someone announces a baby is a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A girl' in cryptics often means any girl's name; here it is SUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal, legal word for offspring or descendants.

clue.text: Animal in motion panicking - too right

indicators.note: panicking letters scatter wildly, ending up in a new order
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a motion is a bowel movement
TOO as printed plus R for right, anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An animal on the move is in a panic, very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motion' reads as movement but is its medical sense, a stool. The rearranged TOO R goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The potoroo is a small Australian marsupial, a rat-kangaroo, so it is one specific creature.

clue.text: Green upset with article for Indian? Could be

indicators.note: something upset is turned over, which in a down clue puts the letters bottom to top

explanation.surface: An environmentalist is annoyed about wording on behalf of an Indian person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like a person, but the question mark and 'could be' signal an example: the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one instance of the great bodies of saltwater, so this is definition by example.

clue.text: Go for champs in broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard over the air, so its sound matters

blocks.note: to champ is to chew noisily

explanation.surface: A call to back the winners on a TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Champs' reads as champions but is the verb to champ, to munch.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for something is to pick or select it from the options.

clue.text: Time con spent in Latin America's not very much

definitions.text: in Latin America's not very much

indicators.note: money that is spent is broken up and scattered

explanation.surface: A trickster's prison time in South America didn't amount to much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' looks like a prison sentence; it and 'con' are only letters. The definition includes 'in Latin America', where the coin is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A centimo is a hundredth of the currency unit in several Spanish-speaking countries, a tiny sum.

clue.text: Swing with nurse in front

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to swing round is to veer

explanation.surface: A child on a swing with a nurse standing ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In front' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'front' the definition. EN is Enrolled Nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: A veneer is a thin surface layer, so figuratively a facade that hides what lies beneath.

clue.text: I returned dirty look Liberal ignored

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came
whatever is ignored is left out altogether

explanation.surface: Someone recalls giving a nasty glare while the Liberal was snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: OGLE reversed is ELGO; dropping L leaves EGO. The definition is the single letter I, the self.
explanation.definitionFit: The ego is a person's sense of self, which the pronoun names in the first person.

clue.text: Didn't prevent Bale getting punished in final

indicators.note: punished letters are knocked about into a new order
one thing in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the final part is the end

explanation.surface: A footballer, Gareth Bale, is booked in a cup final but not stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final' reads as a match but gives END, which holds the rearranged BALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable something is to allow or make it possible, the opposite of blocking it.

clue.text: Hammer old car

blocks.note: a noun here: a heavy wooden mallet for driving wedges or pegs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammer' looks like a verb meaning to bash an old car, but it is a noun for a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A mallet with a big wooden head shares its name with the rounded Volkswagen model of old.

clue.text: Senior embracing sex without agreement, say? It's Trump's forte

indicators.note: say means spoken out loud, so the sound matters rather than the spelling
to be without something is to lack it, so letters are removed
an embrace wraps arms around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: aye means yes, a word of agreement

explanation.surface: A dig at an elderly president's non-consensual behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: Trump is Judd Trump, the English cue-sport champion, not the US president. Aye is spoken the same as the letter I, which is what goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Judd Trump is a world champion at this cue game, so it is the thing he excels at.

clue.text: Sinister country Spain on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A menacing nation, as Spain sees it after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: EIRE plus E runs backwards as EERIE. E for Spain comes from the letters on international car plates.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling in a way that causes unease or fear.

clue.text: Don't believe what was said before but uncertain

indicators.note: letters that are uncertain have no settled order and can be rearranged

blocks.note: short for ditto, used to repeat what came above

explanation.surface: A sceptic refuses to trust an earlier statement.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is the ditto abbreviation, meaning the same as above. 'Uncertain' sounds like the definition but only rearranges 'but'.
explanation.definitionFit: To doubt is to be unconvinced by, or to question the truth of, a claim.

clue.text: Tire out Pole labouring and abruptly slowing down

indicators.note: labouring letters are worked over hard until they fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An exhausted Polish worker suddenly eases off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is a magnetic pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this Italian direction tells players to hold back the tempo at once rather than gradually.

clue.text: Exploits non-British carriers

indicators.note: the prefix non- means without, so a letter is taken away

explanation.surface: Foreign airlines or shipping firms take advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: BUSES loses its B to leave USES. 'Exploits' is a verb here, not heroic deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it, often to one's advantage.

clue.text: Ability parking gets worse after crash

definitions.note: singular noun defining a plural one

indicators.note: a crash smashes things apart, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A driver's parking gets worse following a car accident.
explanation.walkthrough: P comes first and 'worse' is rearranged after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's powers are their faculties or capacities, what they are capable of doing.

clue.text: Private Eye has nothing about singer

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: sweet FA, British slang for nothing at all

explanation.surface: The satirical magazine Private Eye has no story about a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make it look like the British satirical magazine, but it is a detective, PI. Sweet FA means nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Piaf was the French chanteuse famous for songs like La Vie en rose.

clue.text: Over in Florida was this often dried up?

indicators.note: what is in a phrase is contained within its letters
turned over means read the other way, bottom to top in a down clue

blocks.note: four letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A question about whether this feature in Florida used to be dry.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Florida was' backwards to find the answer. 'This' stands for the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a desert valley or streambed that holds water only in the rainy season.

clue.text: Unskilled worker an associate of Bill? That's not true

blocks.note: from the phrase bill and coo, of courting doves

explanation.surface: Someone denies a labourer is a partner of a man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but lovers bill and coo like doves. The answer is a dated and now offensive term.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically this word named a hired labourer from Asia doing heavy manual work for low pay.

clue.text: Tea with a touch of nutmeg added in is extremely fresh

indicators.note: a touch is the lightest contact, so only the very first letter is taken
whatever is put in goes inside something else

blocks.note: a brew is a pot of tea
with and and both mean together

explanation.surface: A cup of tea spiced with nutmeg tastes very fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is not a link here: it supplies its synonym AND, which goes inside the tea along with the nutmeg's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unused and just made is as new as it can be, straight from the maker.
